status: WT lane 2026-11-24, registered before any tour frame was rendered; overrides knowledge/flythrough/villa-policy.json
turn_rate_basis: ASSUMED policy, inside the client-requested 30-45 deg/s comfortable band for an on-screen pan; a full 360 takes 9 s. No published standard claimed.
turn_accel_basis: ASSUMED: yaw rate ramps 0 to 40 deg/s in 0.44 s so no turn starts or stops with a snap
best_view_hold_basis: ASSUMED short pause on the room's best view (the same subject as its still view in knowledge/render-set/views.json)
walk_yaw_rate_basis: ASSUMED policy, 40 deg/s = the 360 turn rate, inside the client band 30-45 (was 30, raised 2026-11-24 so the slow walk through a bend, which was most of the wall-facing walking time, is shorter): walking speed drops wherever the heading would turn faster than this
lookahead_basis: ASSUMED: the camera heading is the direction of the route 1.5 m ahead, so it always looks where it is going
point_wall_clearance_basis: production forward-wall screen (camera_wall_sightline_clearance, 1.0 m); the 360 point keeps every direction clear, so no frame of the turn faces a wall within 1 m
pitch_basis: ASSUMED: the camera looks up the flight while climbing and down the void from the top landing; vertical lens shift is used, as for every still
lens_basis: client decision 2026-11-24: 16 mm for the 360 in small rooms, 24 mm elsewhere; the focal length eases between the two over lens_ease_s (policy, inside the client's 1-1.5 s) while the camera moves or turns, never a cut; smoothstep, so the largest step is 1.5*8/(1.25*24)=0.4 mm per frame

lens_room_rule.basis: a room gets 16 mm when a 24 mm 360 there is wall-dominated in at least this share of its sweep and hold frames (policy; derived by scripts/lens_rooms.py into lens-rooms.json)

exposure_basis: each exposure group (the house day group, each dark room, each garden pan) has its own measured lock; the exposure and white balance move between groups with a moving average of exposure_ease_s so there is no cut
dark_rooms_basis: rooms the audit (v2) finds without glazing visible from the room; each is metered as its own exposure group
turn_rate_variable_basis: ASSUMED policy inside the client's 30-45 deg/s band: the 360 sweeps at 44 deg/s through headings the audit finds wall-dominated from that standing point (tour-points.json yaw_table, widened by one step) and at 30 deg/s through the others, rate changes bounded by turn_accel_deg_s2. 44 not 45 so the measured peak stays under maximum_yaw_rate_deg_s
arc_hold_basis: ASSUMED: half a second on the last heading of a partial look
